checks.name: Clean-clone workspace incl. contract lint/drift and registry parity

scenarios.observed: DiscoveryIntegrationTest: with 26 meals in a kitchen, the oldest matching meal is absent from the first page of 20 but a new server query with q (or category or price filter) returns it; reusing the earlier cursor with changed filters is 422 CURSOR_FILTER_MISMATCH, so clients must restart the query. NEWEST, PRICE_ASC and PRICE_DESC each page through all 23 eligible meals with repeated prices and timestamps exactly once (id tie-breaker). Mutations dropping the tie-breaker and the cursor/filter binding each failed a test. Client behaviour (fresh query on filter change) is verified with the web/native discovery screens (MB-027/MB-031).

Draft, paused and archived meals and all meals of paused or suspended kitchens are excluded from discovery; a paused kitchen's meal detail is 404 while its public profile reports available=false; restoring the kitchen brings its meal back. A mutation removing the ACTIVE-kitchen condition failed the test. The favorites part (unavailable explanation without a broken route) belongs to MB-028 and is re-tested there.

Zone filter returns only kitchens delivering to the zone; date and slot filters return only meals with an orderable slot there and restrict nextSlots to it; availability AVAILABLE/SOLD_OUT/UNAVAILABLE with portions bounded by meal and slot aggregate; past-cutoff slots stop counting; at most five next slots in start order; meal detail uses the same offers; Arabic search ignores diacritics and letter variants, English titles and kitchen names are searchable, wildcards literal; English localization with Arabic fallback; no private fields; zone list active-only, localized, stable paging; invalid sort 400, invalid price range or cursor 422.

findings: Self-review defect fixed before evidence: a Java text block dropped the trailing space before a concatenated SQL predicate (syntax error caught by tests).

Updated IdentityIntegrationTest.public_browsing_stays_anonymous: it asserted 404 only because the route did not exist; it now asserts 200 without redirect, preserving its intent (public route outside authentication).
Proposed defaults recorded: fixed category list; zone filter means delivery to that zone; sorts NEWEST/PRICE_ASC/PRICE_DESC.

Residual: discovery reads kitchen and slot tables as a read model (documented); search uses sequential normalization without a trigram index - revisit with realistic volumes (EXPLAIN) before pilot; registry cityId filter for zones not implemented (no city entity).
